quick.topic: Group days in the right time zone
quick.summary: Why your daily numbers don’t match, and how to group days correctly.
quick.takeaway: Convert to the reporting time zone first. Then group by day.

parts.title: Group days in the right time zone

beats.line: My daily sign ups never match the marketing team’s numbers. Which is wrong?

board.text: Group days in the right time zone

beats.line: Which clock are the times stored in?
The database clock, I think. Not ours.
Your days start at the wrong hour. Sign ups near midnight land on the wrong day.
Convert each time to the time zone your team reports in.

board.text: 1  Convert to the reporting time zone

beats.line: Then group by day, and check one day against a known count.
Is that worth it for a small difference?
Launches near midnight shift days. And two counts for one day lose trust.
So I convert to our reporting time zone, then group by day.
Now each day means the same day for everyone.

quiz.question: Your daily totals differ from another team’s, as if the days start a few hours apart. What is a likely cause?
options: Times are stored in a different time zone from your local day
The other team’s dashboard refreshes more often
The other team rounds its totals
quiz.explanation: If times are stored in another time zone, events near midnight land on the wrong day.

quiz.question: Stored times should be converted to the time zone your team reports in before grouping them by day.
quiz.explanation: Otherwise events near midnight are counted on the wrong day.
